q: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by _____ in 1820.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by Oersted in 1820. Do not trade Oersted for Ampere or Faraday.

q: According to the right-hand rule, if the thumb points along the wire in the direction of the current, the direction of the fingers will give the direction of the _____.
e: Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B. According to the right-hand rule, if the thumb points along the wire in the direction of the current, the direction of the fingers will give the direction of the magnetic field. Electric field or force is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic lines of force around a straight wire carrying a current are _____.
e: The magnetic lines of force around a straight wire carrying a current are closed circular loops. Straight parallel lines or elliptical loops is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic lines of force around a current-carrying wire are in a plane _____ to the wire.
e: The magnetic lines of force around a current-carrying wire are in a plane perpendicular to the wire. Do not trade perpendicular for parallel or at a 45-degree angle.

q: If the current flowing through a wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will be _____.
e: If the current flowing through a wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will be randomized. Unchanged or reversed is not this quantity.

q: A solenoid is a _____ coil of wire.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire. Do not trade cylindrical for rectangular or spherical.

q: The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a bar magnet. Do not trade bar magnet for horseshoe magnet or ring magnet.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction, that end will be a _____ pole.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction, that end will be a south pole. Do not trade south for north or neutral.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction, that end will be a _____ pole.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction, that end will be a north pole. Do not trade north for south or neutral.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the forefinger points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field. Do not trade magnetic field for electric current or motion.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the second finger points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the second finger points in the direction of the electric current. Do not trade electric current for magnetic field or force.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the motion or force. Magnetic field or electric current is not this quantity.

q: When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on that particle is perpendicular to both _____ and _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on that particle is perpendicular to both B and v and _____. Do not trade B and v for E and I or F and I.

q: If a negatively charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on it will be in the _____ direction compared to a positively charged particle.
e: Thomson showed cathode rays are negative. The particle was later named the electron. If a negatively charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on it will be in the opposite direction compared to a positively charged particle. Do not trade opposite for same or perpendicular.

q: A solenoid can be used in an electrical device such as an electric motor that converts electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid can be used in an electrical device such as an electric motor that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. Do not trade mechanical for chemical or thermal.
